modelName: CT unwrapped-diagram and SSPz geometry reference
profileDisplayConvention: Selected-state and all-360-state SSPz screen/600-dpi painters share one native-sample straight-line path. All original calculated z coordinates and values are used, with no display resampling, spline, smoothing, or point/state decimation. The log-tail display omits values below 0.01, breaks paths across those samples, and joins retained points in log10 coordinates. Model calculation, normalization, coordinates, width metrics, and numerical model version are unchanged.
purpose: Visualize acquired-row geometry separately from an ideal axial response using Taguchi and Aradate (1998) Eq. (6) rectangular filter interpolation. The response fixes a thin object and moves the reconstruction plane; 360 curves change the object position within one helical table feed. This is not complete image reconstruction or scanner-specific nominal-thickness prediction.

referenceImplementation.note: Historical baseline only: the named Python reference and full-scan fixture use the former fixed-plane candidate-kernel model. They do not validate the current thick-slice response. Current longitudinal filtering follows Taguchi Eq. (6): reselect adjacent acquired candidates at every resampling z position, linearly interpolate, then apply the normalized finite rectangular-weight sum. Geometry and row apertures remain idealized; complete FBP, scanner-specific weights, and finite bead diameter are excluded. Current browser axial response additionally uses shared finite-channel acquisition; historical fixture agreement does not validate that extension.

scanCalculationConvention: Direct views cover 0 <= beta < 360 degrees. Fan-beam complementary angles use beta+180 degrees+2gamma and their two acquired angular neighbors. Each local resampling coordinate z_f has its own direct/complementary adjacent-candidate selection and normalized linear weights. Angular branches are convexly combined and K resampling values equally averaged. The thin object and its acquired row-aperture samples remain fixed while the reconstruction plane z_r moves. Linear aggregation of the rebracketed piecewise-linear response is used before the finite shifted sum; this is not postconvolution of the former fixed-plane candidate kernel. Browser T sets rectangular averaging width FW; FWHM remains an output. The direct-only comparator omits complementary samples but uses the same moving-plane/filter response definition.
angleConvention: The diagram uses a model-relative tube angle beta with 0 degrees at the top and 360 degrees at the bottom. It is not a measured absolute tube angle. The drawn endpoint at 360 degrees closes the displayed helix period but is not double-counted in SSPz integration.
overlayConvention: The overlay samples 360 fixed-object positions within one table feed. Each curve fixes that object and moves the reconstruction plane, is individually peak-normalized, and uses z_reconstruction-z_object without peak or centroid alignment. All states and all calculated z samples are rendered. Center panels share a >=10% derived horizontal domain; the cone-on log-tail panel uses values >=1%. Display thresholds do not truncate the calculated or exported response.
candidateDisplayConvention: The all-N-row direct and complementary acquired-view trajectories and geometric coordinates are unchanged. Cone-off uses q=1 and a 180-degree complementary angle; cone-on uses fan-angle correspondence and each acquired family's own distance scaling. T and FW do not remove the displayed row population. Section 2B markers/weights and Section 2C gaps refer to local FW=0 interpolation at the selected central position, not all acquired samples contributing across a thick-slice filter. The geometry reference plane passes through the object position selected for SSPz. Same acquired samples may reappear in different angular correspondences; displayed counts are not independent data counts.
acquisitionGeometryFigureConvention: The Section 3C introductory figure is a pre-weight acquisition-geometry display for the currently inspected state. It shows a not-to-scale orthographic focal-spot helix, target plane, one direct acquired view, the two acquired complementary views bracketing the ideal beta plus 180 degrees plus 2 gamma angle, and every detector-row center mapped to the longitudinal line through the evaluation point. Nine representative row rays are drawn in the 3-D panel only for legibility; the adjacent longitudinal panel and numerical calculation retain all rows. A physical detector plane is not inferred because detector-to-isocenter distance is not an input. Color, opacity, and line width encode geometric role only. Circle and triangle markers identify candidates nearest the target plane for explanation; they do not assert use or weight. Schaller AAI h(z), weight normalization, filtering, and backprojection are not applied in this figure.
weightDisplayConvention: Section 2B fixed-size circle/triangle markers and saturation encode normalized local FW=0 endpoint weights at the selected central plane, including angular branch weights. Contributions sharing referenceViewIndex, absoluteViewIndex, and detector row are summed before drawing one opaque glyph. Distinct physical samples at coincident coordinates remain separate. Both family roles are retained if one acquired sample acts as direct and complementary, shown by a small circle inside a triangle. Hue identifies detector row; only trajectory lines use multiply blending to indicate overlap, with opacity and stroke width reduced by sqrt(24/max(24,N)) and a minimum stroke width. Blended line color is neither a new detector row nor a numerical weight. These are not the aggregated thick-slice filter weights. Equal-z ties share endpoint weight as an explicit idealized convention.
allCandidateAxialSpreadConvention: For every direct acquired view beta, the candidate set contains all N detector-row centres in that direct view and all N row centres in each distinct acquired view immediately below and above the ideal complementary angle. A repeated lower-and-upper physical view is included only once, yielding 2N points for an exactly acquired complementary angle and 3N points otherwise. If z-k are the candidate positions, z-bar is their arithmetic mean, and M is their count, the displayed value is sqrt(sum((z-k minus z-bar) squared)/M) in millimetres. It uses no interpolation weight, nearest-candidate selection, support threshold, detector-row aperture variance, or configured slice thickness T. The value is invariant under a common longitudinal translation, so reconstruction-plane position s is not repeated as a second axis. The off/on curves use the same beta and millimetre axes.
internalCandidateAuditConvention: The former computeSsp fixed-plane kernel remains a local-FW0 geometry/legacy numerical diagnostic. Its moments and selected-candidate counts are not interpreted as all thick-slice contributors and are not exported as filtered-response variances.
momentConvention: The former mean(M2)+T^2/12 identity belongs only to the historical fixed-plane-kernel plus continuous width-T rectangle model. It is not an acceptance identity for the fixed-object moving-plane response or the finite-K Taguchi filter. Current filtered width and standard-deviation outputs are computed from the new response.
numericalRasterizationConvention: The current fixed-object response evaluates acquired ideal row apertures and adjacent interpolation as a piecewise-linear function of reconstruction-plane z, combines angular views by linearity, and evaluates the finite K shifted resampling sum. The output grid is shared across states and cone conditions; the requested count is a minimum. No T-wide post-average or old fixed-plane profile rasterization is used to form the new default output. Numerical acceptance requires comparison to direct per-view, per-z, per-filter-position evaluation and K/grid convergence.
complementaryPairConvention: The primary 180LI SSPz path is exact only within the declared idealized acquisition model. Its continuous complementary angle uses the second intersection of the source-to-evaluation-point line with the source orbit. For each acquired angular neighbor, all direct-side and complementary-side detector-row samples are merged and the adjacent candidates around each local z_f are used, allowing DD, DC, CD, or CC types while retaining equal-distance ties and exact matches. The two branch kernels are combined by the ideal angle's linear fraction between the acquired neighbors. The absolute-order D-n-to-C-n and C-n-to-D-n-plus-one spans remain separate diagnostics and are not averaged as an unvalidated redundancy rule. The shared linear detector-channel readout is now included; scanner-specific redundancy weights, cone-beam weights, z-filter calibration, and backprojection remain outside scope.

filterInterpolation.filterSamplesMeaning: requested minimum odd count; actual K may increase and is recorded separately
filterInterpolation.filterSamplesAccuracyGuard: FW/K <= rowWidth*(1-radius/sourceRadius)/8; required odd K > 2049 causes a precision-limit error with no result
filterInterpolation.operation: At each z_f, reselect adjacent acquired direct/complementary row samples in each angular branch, linearly interpolate, combine angular branches, and average K values equally. Acquired candidates outside FW can be used to bracket positions inside FW.
filterInterpolation.thicknessMapping: Browser v9: FW=T, configured thickness is the rectangular averaging width; FWHM is an output, not fitted. No scanner calibration.
filterInterpolation.legacyInitialization: Old browser independent widths are replaced by configured T with a visible migration notice; low-level numerical API retains explicit independent-width reproduction.

selectedProfileDisplay: The final full-width selected-angle SSPz appears once in playback panel (c), with FWHM, FWTM and a 600-dpi PNG export keyed to the movie angle. Section 3 contains the all-360 overlay only. Numerical profiles and exports are unchanged.
